title: Tenant-aware QoS negotiator for latency/throughput tradeoffs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware QoS Negotiator that dynamically mediates per-tenant latency budgets and throughput commitments across the prefill/decode pipeline. The Negotiator will combine three levers: (1) scheduling policy for micro-phase splitting and hedging, (2) kernel-selection hints (e.g., quantized fast-path vs accuracy-preserving kernel), and (3) attention-aware optimizations (sparsity probes and KV cache reuse signals). The goal is to let tenants declare latency SLO bands and optional throughput minima, and have the runtime automatically choose a per-request composite policy that optimizes global throughput while meeting high-priority tenants' latency budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator accepts per-tenant QoS profile containing: latency_budget_ms (p50/p95), throughput_commitment_tps, priority_weight.
Scheduler produces per-request policy decisions: split_count (micro-phase), hedging_flag, kernel_hint, attention_probe_profile.
End-to-end experiments show <=5% p95 latency SLO violations for high-priority tenants under mixed load (mix: 10% high-latency-sensitive, 70% best-effort, 20% bursty) compared to baseline scheduler.
Global throughput improves by >=8% (tokens/sec) at equivalent p50 compared to a static fairness policy under representative production traces.
Integration tests exercising kernel fallbacks and cache reuse paths pass deterministically in CI (no flakiness >1%).
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant QoS decisions in Console (route-level breakdown) and ties decisions to kernel selection and attention probes.
Rollout can be disabled by a feature-flag and falls back to current prefilling decode arbiter without state loss.
test_plan: Unit tests for negotiator decision logic (boundary values for budgets, tie-breaking).
Simulated multi-tenant load tests using production anonymized traces (5-day trace replay) with metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, kernel-switch rate, hedging events.
A/B experiment on a canary cluster comparing current arbiter vs Negotiator for 3 days with 1% traffic, then 5% to 20% conditional on violation rate.
Failure injection tests: kernel slow-path degradation, KV cache misses, node OOM—ensure graceful fallback and preserved high-priority SLOs.
End-to-end integration test in staging that verifies Console shows decision breadcrumbs for at least one tenant and that rollback works.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) feature-flagged implementation in runtime-1.22 on a small dedicated fleet; 2) 1% canary for 72h with automated SLO checks; 3) expand to 10% if SLO violations <1.5x baseline; 4) enable multi-tenant weighted scheduling cluster-wide and monitor for 7 days before full rollout. If kernel-switch churn exceeds threshold, revert to kernel-hinted static policy and investigate.

2025-02-28 - Performance results: preliminary staging run shows 12% throughput uplift in best-effort dominated traces but 2.3% p95 regressions for mid-priority tenant — investigating tie-breaker weight scaling.
2025-03-03 - Security: KMS/secret access not needed. Confirmed security_review_required=false. Still coordinating with infra on feature-flag rollout mechanics.

2025-03-05 - Diego Alvarez: Ran 72h canary at 1% traffic. No high-priority SLO violations. Observed kernel-switch churn spikes during global bursts; added smoothing guard to suppress kernel switching if recent switch_rate > 0.08/s.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive hedging reduces p95 but increases token cost and kernel switching. We will expose tenant profile knobs (aggressive/lenient) for power users. Implementation will prefer widening micro-phase splits over immediate hedging where attention_probe indicates high KV cache reuse potential.
outstanding_risks: Kernel-switch churn may amplify tail latencies if not smoothed; attention sparsity probes require low-overhead sampling to avoid becoming a source of latency; multi-tenant tie-breaking must not starve low-priority background workloads beyond contractual throughput commitments.
